title: Retry-safe network pool creation against the SDDC Manager 9.0 API
prompt:
The `netpool` package is a dependency-free Go client for the VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 SDDC Manager network pool API. It covers the two operations recorded in `docs/contract.json`, `getNetworkPool` and `createNetworkPool`, and nothing else may go on the wire. That contract is derived from the SDDC Manager OpenAPI document at tag 9.0.0.0 of the vmware/vcf-api-specs repository, and `docs/official_sources.json` records where it came from. Between them they are the authority on the API's shape; do not go by memory of the 9.1 revision, which differs.

Two things are wrong in `netpool/client.go`.

First, `EnsureNetworkPool` is not safe to repeat and not safe to retry. It goes straight to `createNetworkPool`, so re-running a provisioning pass, or retrying after a failure whose outcome is unknown, either leaves a second pool behind or fails outright on a name the previous attempt already claimed. A create whose response was lost is the hard case: it may well have taken effect. The `idempotency` section of the contract sets out what is required, including what `EnsureResult.Created` has to mean and when a failure must still be reported to the caller. At most one create request may leave the client per call.

Second, the create request does not carry the wire shape the contract describes. The request body is built from the read model, so properties the 9.0.0.0 schemas mark `readOnly` are sent anyway, and the one optional property is put on the wire empty when the caller left it unset instead of being omitted from the JSON entirely.

Fix both in `netpool/client.go`, using only the standard library.

Run `python3 tests/verify.py` to check your work. It builds and vets the module, then runs the suite under `go test -race` against a loopback double that logs every request it receives and measures it against the contract; no VMware endpoint is involved. Treat `docs/`, `go.mod`, `netpool/client_test.go`, `netpool/mock/mock.go` and `tests/` as fixed, and make your changes in `netpool/client.go`.
